# Sourcera Audit — Coverage Matrix

**Phase 0 / Prompt 0.3** — Master Spec v7.1.0 baseline. One row per feature in `FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` (968 rows). Cell values: `✅` clearly satisfied · `⚠` partial · `❌` silent · `n/a` structurally inapplicable. Phase 0 seeds the matrix via class-based heuristics with anchor / name overrides; later phases tighten cells via full adversarial reads. Every non-`✅` cell carries a one-line evidence note in the trailing `evidence` column per `Audit_Prompts.md → Coverage Matrix Format`.

**Seeding doctrine.** Phase 0 is allowed to err toward `⚠`. Override rules promote `⚠` → `✅` only when the feature's primary or secondary anchor unambiguously satisfies the convention (e.g., anchor in §5.* satisfies `rbac`; anchor referencing Appendix J satisfies `enums`; §31/§32 anchors satisfy `webhook`/`api`; §3.7.* satisfies `empty_state`/`loading_state`/`error_state`; §38 satisfies `mobile_parity`; §37 satisfies `accessibility`/`i18n`; §40.2/§44/§47 satisfy `retention`/`performance_budget`/`residency`; §M.4/§M.5/§50.17 satisfy `ci_gate_coverage`; §51 satisfies `posthog_events`/`observability`). Cells marked `n/a` reflect structural inapplicability (e.g., third-party `integration_surface` rows have no platform RBAC; `engine_concept` rows have no UI states). All `n/a` cells carry a justification template.

**Authored Extension status.** F-AE-* rows seed `authored_extension_status` from the AE Ledger flag in their `one_line_summary` (`pending` → `⚠`, `ratified` → `✅`). Non-AE rows are `n/a`.

**Evidence column convention.** For every cell that is not `✅`, the evidence column contains `<dim>: <one-line note>`, semicolon-separated. The note seeds Phase-N defect filings: it is intentionally template-grade in Phase 0 (e.g., "Appendix J registration not yet cross-checked") so later passes can sharpen the note with line numbers and cite the missing element.

### Phase 1.5 Update (2026-04-30) — §4.6 Audit & Logging Entities sub-prompt

The Phase 1.5 §4.6 sub-prompt deep-read (`PHASE1.5_FINDINGS.md`) filed 14 D-1.5 defects against the Audit Event entity (§4.6.1), the §4.6.1.1 retention/DSAR/state-machine block, the §6.7 Audit Logging surface, the §40.2 retention contract, the Appendix J `audit_event_action_type` registry, and the §50.5 Ops-Tagged Audit Actor extension — **5 P0 / 4 P1 / 3 P2 / 2 P3.** The five P0 findings split between (a) D-1.5-001 — the §4.6.1 `changes` JSON has no bearer-secret-exclusion clause and would today accept a write of `{"password_hash":{"old_value":"...","new_value":"..."}}` against `entity_type='user'`, leaking the secret to every Org Admin via the Audit Surface — and (b) D-1.5-002 / D-1.5-003 / D-1.5-004 / D-1.5-005 — twelve audit `action` strings emitted across §4.6.1.1, §6.7.4, §10.16, §2.8, §22.20.2, §22.20.7, §25.2 are unregistered in any Appendix-J namespace and would today fail the `audit_event_action_enum_union_validator`, breaking every emit path that uses them. The §4.6.1 entity itself has a robust state-machine declaration ("append-only and immutable; no state machine"), a comprehensive DSAR cascade (pseudonymization-in-place; payload retained verbatim per §6.8.5 row #1), and a passing residency partition rule — those convention checks all pass. The defect concentration is on the registry surfaces (Appendix J under-coverage), the §6.7 schema drift from the v7.0.0 §4.6.1 D-1V-008 / D-1V-010 rewrite, and the §40.2 missing AuditEvent retention row.

### Phase 3.2 Update (2026-05-04) — §5.11 Feature Access Matrix Coverage sub-prompt

The Phase 3.2 §5.11 deep-read (`PHASE3.2_FINDINGS.md`) filed 29 D-3.2 defects against the §5.11 Feature Access Matrix — 0 P0 / 23 P1 / 2 P2 / 4 P3. The findings split into four clusters: (A) structural gaps in the matrix dimensions (6 defects), (B) promised §5.11 rows not present in the body (10 reverse-pass defects citing §22 / §27 / §32 / §48 / §50 explicit "is updated to add row" commitments), (C) major plan-gated user-facing capabilities absent from the matrix (7 defects), (D) documentation drift (6 defects).

The matrix is structurally role × capability with no plan-tier dimension, despite §34.1.3 line 27693 directing §5.11 to "(b) gate per-capability access to plan tiers per the Entitlement Matrix in §34.8." Plan-tier gating is encoded in inline row-label strings using literal Title-Case plan names (per Phase 14.9.1's 27-location backlog), which drift silently when plan names change. ### Phase 3.3 Update (2026-05-04) — §6.1–§6.6 Identity, Authentication & Authorization sub-prompt

The Phase 3.3 §6.1–§6.6 deep-read (`PHASE3.3_FINDINGS.md`) filed 37 D-3.3 defects against §6.1 Authentication Architecture, §6.2 MFA, §6.3 Session Management, §6.4 Domain Governance, §6.5 Guest Users & SSO Bypass, and §6.6 API Token Authentication — 0 P0 / 26 P1 / 11 P2 / 0 P3. The findings split into six clusters mirroring the §6 sub-section partition: A §6.1 (5), B §6.2 (9), C §6.3 (7), D §6.4 (7), E §6.5 (3), F §6.6 (6).

Three structural failures dominate. (1) **Three independent token-scope vocabularies coexist and disagree** (D-3.3-032). §6.6.3 ships `bidding:write` / `evaluation:read` / `scoring:write` / `responses:read` / `analytics:read` (5 scopes); Appendix J `API Token Scopes` registers a disjoint 11-scope `read:requirements` / … / `admin:billing` set; §32 endpoint contracts emit additional values (`write:workspaces`, `admin:workspaces`, `export:billing`, `export:kb`) that appear in neither. Zero values intersect across (a) §6.6.3 ↔ (b) Appendix J. (2) **Five Appendix-I error codes referenced from §6 are not registered in Appendix I** (`plan_upgrade_required`, `session_expired`, `plan_limit_exceeded`, `token_revoked`, `token_expired`); a sixth (`domain_already_claimed`) is registered under the canonical `m6_*` prefix and §6.4 emits the bare name. (3) **§6.2 MFA prose, §4.2.1 Org schema, and Appendix J `MFA Enforcement Levels` ship three different representations of the same concept** (D-3.3-008): §6.2.2 `mfa_enforcement_required` (Boolean implicit); §4.2.1 `mfa_required_org_wide` (Boolean explicit); Appendix J `off` / `optional` / `required` (ternary enum, zero consumers). The §6.2.2 / §4.2.1 / §6.2.3 14-day grace window is a three-way contradiction (D-3.3-009).

§6.3 Session Management is silent on every dimension the audit checklist requires — refresh semantics (D-3.3-016), revocation-propagation latency (D-3.3-017), session state machine (D-3.3-018), Convex outage handling (D-3.3-019), mobile divergence (D-3.3-020). §6.4 Domain Governance ships a 10-line description that contradicts §48.6's 1,200-line authoritative authoring (D-3.3-023 — recommend §6.4 collapse to a thin pointer). §6.5 silent on cross-Org guest identity reuse (D-3.3-029 — SSO-bypass vector); silent on guest interaction with `mfa_enforcement_level=required` (D-3.3-030).

### Phase 3.4 Update (2026-05-04) — §6.7 Audit Logging walk sub-prompt

The Phase 3.4 §6.7 walk (`PHASE3.4_FINDINGS.md`) filed 7 D-3.4 defects against §6.7.1 Audit Log Scope, §6.7.2 Audit Log Structure, §6.7.3 Retention Policy by Plan, §6.7.4 Audit Log Access — 3 P0 / 3 P1 / 1 P2 / 0 P3. The prompt's explicit P0 trigger ("P0 for any audit-log integrity gap") plus rule-based mapping to Severity Definitions (c) "violates a hard regulatory requirement (... audit-log integrity)" anchored three findings at P0: integrity protection (D-3.4-001), the missing `audit_event_high_impact_actions` registry that the integrity scan depends on (D-3.4-002), and the §6.7.1 line 9517 explicit exclusion of failed-login attempts from the audit log (D-3.4-003 — SOC 2 CC6.1 / NIST 800-53 AU-2 compliance violation).

Three structural failures dominate. (1) **Cryptographic integrity protection is partial.** §6.7 promises "append-only and immutable" but the only enforcement is application-layer; hash-chain protection at §42.6.1 covers ONLY the "high-impact" subset (~100k rows/month — fraction of corpus), the registry that names the subset is undefined (D-3.4-002), and the §50.2.4 ¶4 break-glass DB write path bypasses the application-layer validator entirely. AuditEvent has no parallel to §4.7.2 VendorDisqualificationRecord's `audit_chain_hash` / `chain_position` columns. (2) **Authentication-anomaly visibility is absent.** §6.7.1 actively excludes failed login attempts from the audit log; §6.6.4 lockout policy emits no audit event for the lockout itself; §6.5 SSO and §6.6 password-auth flows emit zero audit events for any login outcome; Appendix C registers no `security.*` family events (suspicious login, account_locked, mfa_factor_changed, new_device_login, session_revoked_by_admin). The §51 PostHog `auth_*` taxonomy is a product-analytics surface with separate consent / retention rules and does not substitute. (3) **Audit-log surfacing access matrix is inconsistent across five sections.** §6.7.4, §36.2, §5.2.1.4, §50.5.4, §50.5.5 each describe parts of the same access matrix and disagree on Billing Admin / Workspace Owner / Team Owner / Ops-actor visibility. §36.2 line 29714 additionally inline-restates the retention curve with the stale `Business` plan-tier name (replaced by Starter / Growth / Scale in the v6.0.0 → v7.0.0 rewrite) and silently omits Solo (D-3.4-006).

The console-bridge layer carries per-event `console_bridge.dlq_entered` / `console_bridge.reconciliation_summary` (D-1.6-003 P1 forwarded for Appendix C / Appendix G registration) but no aggregate failure-storm detector — D-3.4-007 P2 lands a §25.2.6 "Console-Bridge Failure Storm Detection" sub-section with the `console_bridge.dlq_storm` event paired to D-3.4-004's Appendix C Console-Bridge-Anomaly-Domain Events sub-section.

### Phase 3.5 Update (2026-05-04) — §6.8 DSAR / GDPR / Right-to-Erasure walk sub-prompt

The Phase 3.5 §6.8 walk (`PHASE3.5_FINDINGS.md`) filed 38 D-3.5 defects against §6.8.1 Right of Access, §6.8.2 Right to Erasure on Deprovisioning, §6.8.3 Right to Erasure on Account Closure, §6.8.4 DSAR Cascade, §6.8.4.1 Cascade Pseudonymization Pattern, §6.8.5 Audit-Integrity Exemption, §6.8.6 DSAR Operational SLA, plus the §33.4 / §33.5 / §33.9 / §40.2 / §45.1 cross-walks — 6 P0 / 19 P1 / 10 P2 / 3 P3. The prompt's explicit "highest-stakes audit" guidance combined with severity rule (c) ("violates a hard regulatory requirement (GDPR right-to-erasure, US/EU data-residency lock, audit-log integrity)") anchored six findings at P0: Articles 16/18/20/21 silence (D-3.5-001), missing DSARRequest entity blocking SLA observability (D-3.5-002), AIOperation cascade contradiction between §6.8.4.1 Pattern B and §4.8.1 AC #12 on a financial-record audit row (D-3.5-003), missing §6.9 deprovisioning workflow (D-3.5-004), missing subject-verification protocol blocking the SLA clock-start (D-3.5-005), and the residency-silent cascade walker risking unlawful third-country PII transfer (D-3.5-006).

Three structural failures dominate. (1) **GDPR Chapter III is two-thirds unimplemented.** §6.8 line 9554 explicitly enumerates only Article 15 and Article 17. Articles 16 (rectification), 18 (restriction), 20 (portability as a discrete transmission-to-controller right), 21 (objection), and 22 (automated decisions) are silent or partial; no `restricted_processing` state on User; no rectification API; no automated-decision human-review path despite Match-Score and AI-Scoring being automated decisions about subjects (D-3.5-001, D-3.5-025). CCPA / LGPD / UK-GDPR coverage is one-citation-deep in §6.8.6 line 9748 with no implementation (D-3.5-013). (2) **The DSAR cascade prescription is internally contradictory on financial-record entities.** §6.8.4.1 line 9688 prescribes Pattern B (preserve UUID FK; pseudonymize User row in-place) on AIOperation citing field name `submitter_user_id`. §4.8.1 AC #12 line 7982 prescribes scrub `actor_id`. The actual field on §4.8.1 is `actor_id`, not `submitter_user_id`. §6.8.5 row #3 line 9715 cites `submitter_user_id` / `signed_by_user_id` / `accepter_user_id` — three field names, two of which do not exist on the entities they cite (§4.8.1 has `actor_id`; §4.8.5 has `filed_by_user_id`, not `accepter_user_id`). A junior engineer reading any one prescription would build the wrong financial-record cascade (D-3.5-003 P0, D-3.5-016 P1, D-3.5-019 P1). (3) **The DSAR SLA is unbuildable as written.** DSARRequest has no entity table in §4 (D-3.5-002 P0); the verification protocol that starts the SLA clock is undefined (D-3.5-005 P0); the cascade walker is residency-silent (D-3.5-006 P0); the §6.8.6 SLA references five fields not declared anywhere; the cascade emits five AuditEvents and one PostHog event none of which are registered in Appendix C / G / J (D-3.5-017 P1).

The SLA-singleton enforcement gap also lands a P1: §6.8.6 AC #2 declares CI gate `dsar_sla_single_source_of_truth`, but §33.4 / §33.9 / §40.2 / §6.8.4 line 9645 currently inline-restate the 30-day window without citing §6.8.6 — gate would fail on existing rows (D-3.5-009 P1). The `§45.1 financial-record exemption` reference invoked from five §40.2 rows (BuyerReferral, Pro Trial Seat, VendorOptOutRecord, PromotedListing, FeaturedPlacement) is a broken pointer — §45.1 body has no such exemption clause; the exemption authority lives in §6.8.5 (D-3.5-038 P1).

KB-derived embeddings cascade is partial: §22.3.1 covers entry-level erasure (vector + BM25 purged co-transactionally). User-author DSAR is OK (Pattern B preserves `created_by` FK; embeddings encode body content not author identity). Third-party DSAR (subject named in KB body but not a Sourcera account-holder) is silent — the dense vector encodes the subject's name and §6.8 has no body-redaction sweep (D-3.5-012 P1). The §40.2 VerificationReviewRecord row has the only third-party-DSAR clause in the spec (line 30573); the precedent is not generalized.

Cross-Console Bridge Event cascade is closed by the D-1V-012 / D-1V3-001 remediation (Pattern B on `created_by`/`updated_by` UUID FKs; Pattern A inside `payload_json`; CI gate `bridge_event_dsar_cascade_field_partition`). Salt-rotation re-pseudonymization conflicts with the embedded `payload_json` pseudonyms — §6.8.5 AC #3 rewrites the User row's hash but the `payload_json` Pattern-A-embedded string remains the OLD hash; audit-chain forensics break (D-3.5-032 P2).

Marketplace Discovery aggregates' k-anonymity floor is wired at the entity level (§4.4.12 nightly sweep, §4.4.18 24-hour recompute, §4.4.16 cohort flip) but the §6.8.4 cascade walker contract does not directly trigger the recompute — a 24-hour leak window exists between erasure and the nightly sweep (D-3.5-031 P2).

## Verification (Self-Challenge Pass)

This matrix was produced by class-based heuristic seeding plus anchor / name-keyword overrides. Phase-0 seeding is intentionally conservative — every cell that is not `✅` carries an evidence template in the trailing `evidence` column so Phase-1+ defect filings can promote findings without re-deriving the seed.

**Known Phase-0 limitations (carry into PHASE0_FINDINGS.md):**

1. The seeding pass did not perform per-feature line-by-line reads. Many `⚠` cells will resolve to `✅` once Phase 1+ verifies the entity field tables, AC blocks, state-machine tables, API contracts, and webhook contracts that Master Spec §4–§51 actually contains.
2. The seeding pass treats `engine_concept` rows as having no UI states (`empty_state` / `loading_state` / `error_state` = `n/a`). A subset of `engine_concept` rows do have UI surface implications (e.g., F-091 Evaluation Pulse Event) — Phase 3 (UX audit) will tighten these to `⚠` or `✅`.
3. Cells default to `⚠` rather than `❌` when the convention is structurally applicable, because Phase 0 cannot disprove presence on a quick read. Phase 1+ will demote `⚠` → `❌` when a full read confirms silence.
4. Authored Extension status is read from the inventory's `[AE: pending]` / `[AE: ratified]` flags. The AE Ledger is the canonical source — Phase 14 (Cross-Document Drift) will re-validate every AE row against `_integration/AUTHORED_EXTENSIONS_LEDGER.md`.

**Sample of 5 random features for hostile-reviewer confirmation** (full sample documented in `PHASE0_VERIFY.md`): per-feature spot-checks were performed against Master Spec section anchors during seeding. Where a quick read showed the seeded value mismatched a hostile-reviewer reading, the override table tightened the cell. Remaining `⚠` cells are intentionally left for Phase 1+ to resolve.

The pre-existing D-V6-002 / D-V6-003 / D-V6-006 / D-V6-007 cluster is remediated and NOT re-filed.

Three structural failures dominate. (1) **§34.16 plan-tier list is stale** (D-MD-001) — preamble line 29918 enumerates a 5-tier model (Free / Starter / Growth / Scale / Enterprise) that the v7.1.0 Phase 14.9 program superseded with the 6-tier Solo-inclusive model. Substantively Solo plans don't transact §34.16 SKUs, so the omission is enumeration-stale, not eligibility-stale; CLAUDE.md §16 Phase 14.9.2 backlog catalogues this defect class as P1. (2) **Quality-floor anti-spam linkage is incomplete** (D-MD-007) — §34.16.4 #2 declares the `quality_floor` gate as "Verification Tier < Basic or anti-spam flags", but the canonical 10-condition gate authored at §4.4.19 *Eligibility Gate* (lines 5705–5805) plus §27.11.1 design principle 5 plus §27.11.6 G7 includes TWO additional gates absent from §34.16: KB Health Score (§22.5) ≥ 60.00, and `eligibility_closed_bid_count_90d_snapshot ≥ 1`. The §34.16.7 error message `promoted_listing_quality_floor_failed` HTTP 403 carries the same partial coverage. Engineers reading §34.16 alone would build a runtime gate that fails to enforce the canonical contract — the audit prompt's CHECK 3 explicitly fails on this. (3) **Webhook payload k=5 anonymization bypass** (D-MD-005) — `promoted_listing.auction_settled` payload `winners: [{org_id, paid_cents, rank, promoted_listing_id}]` is delivered to "Yes (bidders + winners)", exposing every winner's identity and paid amount to every bidder including losers. The §34.16.1 *Anonymization* k=5 floor protects digest aggregation but the per-event webhook bypasses it; an adversarial bidder can submit a low bid solely to receive the auction_settled payload. The asymmetry is not rationalized in the spec; either the §27.11.1 design principle 4 ("k=5 anonymization on all aggregated auction / bidder metrics") is violated, or the auction_settled event needs an explicit exemption with rationale.

Two cross-document numerical drifts also surface. (4) **Monthly cap math conflict** (D-MD-002) — §34.16.1 says "1 primary + 4 additional = 5/month/seller"; §27.11.2 #5 says "Scale: 1 base + 4 add-on = 5; Enterprise: 3 base + 4 add-on = 7"; §34.1.2 plan-tier table backs the §27.11.2 reading. §34.16 needs to defer to §34.1.2 for plan-tier base allotment. (5) **k-anonymity floor conflict** (D-MD-020) — §34.16 / §27.11 use k=5 (≥5 distinct bidders); §4.8.12 *Failure Mode #5* and AC #10 use k=3 (cohort floor for revenue deferral). Two distinct floors with two distinct purposes (digest-render anonymity vs revenue-deferral anonymity); both are defensible but neither is named or rationalized as a numerical singleton. Resolution: author named floors `k_anonymity_cohort_floor_render = 5` and `k_anonymity_cohort_floor_revenue_deferral = 3` in §39, cite from §34.16 / §27.11 / §4.8.12 instead of restating.

Cross-reference completeness gaps span the audit prompt's CHECK 6: §34.16 has zero `§27.4` / `§27.3` cross-references for ranking-model integrity (D-MD-011) and zero §3 / UX-token cross-references for badge rendering (D-MD-010). Both gaps are P2 documentation; ranking integrity is enforced in code per §27.11.6 G2 (`ranking_model_no_promoted_features` model-card invariant) but §34.16.4 #2 reads as an unenforced narrative without the cross-link.

### Phase 45 Update (2026-05-08) — §45 Privacy & Abuse Prevention sweep

The Phase 45 single-prompt audit of Master Spec §45 (lines 32584–32631) filed 22 D-45 defects against F-625 (Data Privacy Posture / §45.1), F-626 (Abuse Prevention Controls / §45.2), and F-627 (Marketplace Abuse Escalation Workflow / §45.3) — 0 P0 / 10 P1 / 9 P2 / 3 P3. Findings detailed in `PHASE45_FINDINGS.md`.

**Headline finding.** §45 is ~46 lines for a chapter that should anchor the platform's privacy and abuse-prevention story. Almost every substantive contract lives elsewhere (§4.5.7, §22, §27.8, §27.9, §27.10, §27.11.2, §32.4, §40.2, §42.3.1, §47.4, §48.4.4) and §45 fails to route a reader to those homes. Of the six prompt-defined checks, only one (vendor-opt-out enforcement at §27.10) is mechanically auditable; one (KB content moderation) is genuinely absent from the corpus, not just under-cited at §45.
